s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive subcutaneous node in the axilla with skin infiltration and episodic pain
salient_findings: Slowly growing subcutaneous node in the right axilla
Progressive infiltration of the overlying skin
Erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring 5 × 3 cm
Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm in an 'Indian file pattern'
key_facts: The patient is a woman in her 60s
The subcutaneous node was first noticed 10 years ago
The node has been slowly growing
The patient experienced swelling in the right axilla during pregnancy over 20 years ago
The swelling disappeared with lactation
The patient experienced mild episodic pain in her right axilla during menstrual cycles
A solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque is present in the right axilla
The plaque measures 5 × 3 cm
Histopathology shows dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells are diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles and lined up in an 'Indian file pattern'
Tumor cells have basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm
Immunohistochemistry is positive for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies
Imaging studies show no evidence of primary or secondary tumors

shortlist.label: Hidradenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches histopathology and immunohistochemistry findings, including positive staining for GATA3 and estrogen receptor

shortlist.label: Apocrine carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the presence of apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration and positive immunohistochemistry for GCDFP15 and GATA3

shortlist.label: Mammary analog secretory carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Shares similarities with the case's histopathological and immunohistochemical features, including positivity for GATA3 and estrogen receptor

shortlist.label: Syringomatous carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Could be considered given the tumor's location and histological features, although less likely than apocrine or hidradenocarcinoma

shortlist.label: Microcystic adnexal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible diagnosis due to the tumor's location and histological appearance, but less likely given the specific immunohistochemical profile

shortlist.label: Sclerosing sweat duct carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to the tumor's location and histological features, but less likely than apocrine or hidradenocarcinoma

shortlist.label: Secretory carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Could be a consideration given the tumor's histological features and immunohistochemical profile, although less likely than mammary analog secretory carcinoma

shortlist.label: Carcinoma en cuirasse
shortlist.why_kept: Less likely, but remains a possibility due to the tumor's clinical presentation and location
